title: Herschel/Planck NCTRS Setup
organisation: Herschel/Planck Mission Operations Centre (HMOC), ESA/ESOC (as indicated by the document number; no organisation name is printed)
status_notes: Printed status 'Version 1 - Updated', created and last checked in 11/08/2011, inside FOP issue 3.1 dated 05/09/11 (PDF p. 1). No other issue is in the library.
summary:
A single ground-segment procedure from the Herschel/Planck Flight Operations Plan (FOP, PT-HMOC-OPS-FOP-6001-OPS-OAH). It uses the standard FOP layout: a summary sheet, a flowchart page (an image, not extracted) and six numbered steps. It covers starting and stopping the mission-specific instances of the **NCTRS** (Network Control and TM/TC Router System) on the two NCTRS machines of MCS chains A and B. NCTRS is the ESOC gateway between ground stations and the mission control system; see [NCTRS, NIS and the ground station interface](../scos2000/nctrs-nis.md).

The procedure is built around one constraint: only one NCTRS instance per mission may run on each chain, so at most one Herschel and one Planck NCTRS exist on NCTRS-A and NCTRS-B. For the same reason, the NCTRS OVERVIEW task must never be started there, because it would allow an instance to be started on a machine of the other mission. The operator opens a terminal on a DCR client, enables X display forwarding, and connects to the NCTRS host by telnet. The operator then runs the stop command for the mission (repeated, because clean-up is sometimes incomplete), checks the process list, and runs the start command, after which the NCTRS MMI appears on the client. A final step logs in to the NCTRS MMI. Troubleshooting notes cover an instance that is still running and the missing X display permission.

This is a rare public, concrete example of how NCTRS was operated at ESOC for a SCOS-2000 based mission. It gives no protocol or interface detail.

key_points.text: The objective is starting or stopping NCTRS-A and NCTRS-B. The procedure ensures there is only one NCTRS instance per mission, i.e. one Herschel and one Planck NCTRS per MCS chain (A and B).
The NCTRS OVERVIEW task is not started (and is stopped with 'NCTRSstop OVERVIEW') because it would allow another instance to be started on a machine of the other mission.
The operator works from a DCR client terminal, runs 'xhost +' and connects to the NCTRS host by telnet. The NCTRS MMI then appears on the DCR client's display.

The mission instance is stopped with NCTRSstop Herschel or NCTRSstop Planck. The procedure says to run the command three times because clean-up is sometimes incomplete, and to check with 'ps -ef' that no Herschel or Planck tasks remain.
The mission instance is started with NCTRSstart Herschel or NCTRSstart Planck, after which the NCTRS MMI should appear on the DCR client.
Troubleshooting: if NCTRS does not start, it is probably still running and must be stopped first. If it cannot create displays, the 'xhost +' was probably forgotten before the telnet session.
The last step is a login on the NCTRS MMI. The source prints the host and MMI credentials, which are deliberately not reproduced here.

notes: Four numbered pages; the extraction reports 5 PDF pages, the last of which is empty. The flowchart on PDF p. 2 is an image. The procedure cites no documents, and its reference-file and display fields are empty. The source prints login names and passwords for the NCTRS host and MMI (PDF pp. 3-4); do not reproduce them. Companion procedure from the same FOP in the library: c-gsp-mcs-scos (FOP issue 3.0).
